Built against [wamsoft/krkrz_dev](https://github.com/wamsoft/krkrz_dev) V2.6.5

- **Characters drawn from layers, with blinking eyes and lip-sync**: a World character listed in `charinit.csv` is put together from layers each time it's shown, from outfits, pose variations and faces named in an `_info.txt`, with layers drawn at each World level's size. Its eyes blink by themselves, and its mouth moves with its voice, measured as it plays with the engine's own `WaveSoundBuffer.getSoundLevel`, on every platform (`doc/world.txt`, "Characters Drawn from Layers")
- Tags hold, open, close or flip the eyes and mouth (`eyecloseto`, `eyeflip=3`, `lipflip=4`...), `x<face>` changes the face with the eyes closed, and `charanim.csv` defines animations
- The sample's new World Extension: Animated Character demo, last in the demo menu, with Pip: two outfits, three arm poses, six faces and babbled voice lines, all made by `tools/assets/make_pip.py`
- Extras on the title screen unlock once the new demo has been played too
- Fixed random crashes ("free(): corrupted unsorted chunks", "double free or corruption", 0xC0000374 on Windows): the engine's general memory pool corrupted its heap now and then, so the packages turn it off (`krkrzpoolsize=none` in `krkrz.cf`), and kagex-release does the same for every game unless its `krkrz.cf` sets the option. The Android and iOS builds can't take engine options yet
- kagex-release 0.8.0 downloads the 0.8.0 engines

Everything in this release is listed in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/krkren/kagex/blob/0.8.0/CHANGELOG.md).

On Windows the engine needs OpenGL ES: a graphics driver that supports it, or ANGLE's `libEGL.dll` and `libGLESv2.dll` next to `krkrz.exe`.

The macOS app and tool aren't signed with an Apple Developer ID, so macOS blocks them the first time: open the app from the context menu (Open), or allow it under System Settings > Privacy & Security; for the tool, `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine kagex-release`. The Android APK is signed with a debug key: allow installs from unknown sources, or use `adb install`. The sample's iOS build is for the Simulator; kagex-release signs a game for iPhones and iPads with your own Apple Developer certificate.
